claims.claim: Germani assembled a readable 427-word passage out of the first sentences of 26 different paragraphs of A Game of Thrones totalling 1,897 words.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Compressible Paragraphs', At Sea Journal
claims.quote: built from the first sentences of 26 different paragraphs

claims.claim: Germani's verdict is that Martin is imprecise rather than incompetent as a sentence writer.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Imprecise Sentences', At Sea Journal

claims.claim: Germani argues that flow between sentences, rather than great individual sentences, is the litmus test for a successful author, and that Martin passes it.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Imprecise Sentences', At Sea Journal
claims.quote: Flow between sentences is the litmus test for a successful author

claims.claim: Germani observes Martin shifting into antiquated diction in a passage describing the haunted forest.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Purple Prose in Green and Red', At Sea Journal

claims.claim: Germani argues Martin's writing leaps into a high register when presented with the wordless sensations of nature and violence.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Purple Prose in Green and Red', At Sea Journal

claims.claim: Amalvy and colleagues count 777 characters in the novels for their U2 period, against 199 in the TV show annotations.
claims.source: Amalvy et al., Social Network Analysis and Mining 14 (2024)
claims.quote: there are 777 characters in the novels

claims.claim: Amalvy and colleagues report that 731, or 94 percent, of the novels' characters in their U2 period are named.
claims.source: Amalvy et al., Social Network Analysis and Mining 14 (2024)

claims.claim: Amalvy and colleagues note that their novel interaction data includes memories, because important plot information is frequently revealed through a character thinking of past events.
claims.source: Amalvy et al., Social Network Analysis and Mining 14 (2024)
claims.quote: Note that this does include memories

claims.claim: Germani counts 148,130 sentences in A Song of Ice and Fire.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Zeugma and Literary DNA', At Sea Journal

claims.claim: Germani found roughly 250 examples in A Song of Ice and Fire of a zeugma structure in which one verb governs two comma-separated clauses.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Zeugma and Literary DNA', At Sea Journal

claims.claim: Germani identifies the zeugma structure as one Martin uses for describing sky and weather, with the human body as its most common subject.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Zeugma and Literary DNA', At Sea Journal

claims.claim: Germani finds Martin willing to be culturally anachronistic in dialogue, citing a Lannister line lifted from Robert Frost.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Cultural Anachronism', At Sea Journal
claims.quote: Martin is willing to be anachronistic with his dialogue

claims.claim: Germani reports that one of Theon's chapters in A Dance with Dragons features 33 different speakers.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Line Reading', At Sea Journal

claims.feature: other: introduction formula for a person
claims.claim: Germani finds that Martin's block characterisations follow a fixed order, hitting age, hair, eyes, clothes, and physique.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Block Characterization', in 'Odds and Ends', At Sea Journal
claims.quote: He hits on age, hair, eyes, clothes, and physique

claims.feature: other: introduction formula for a person
claims.claim: Germani defines a block characterisation as the block of description a character receives when first coming on stage.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Block Characterization', in 'Odds and Ends', At Sea Journal
claims.quote: block of description characters receive when they first come on stage
